correctness.rationale: Under the equal-effort independent Poisson model with a fixed common phase, maximizing worst detection is exactly maximizing the minimum total mean. Center the two visits, set q=cos(Δ/2), z=2q²−1 and x=cos φ; the harmonic part divided by 2c is rqx+z(2x²−1). For 0<r<4 the branch minimized at x=−1 runs from q=0 to the unique positive junction q₀ given by rq₀=4(2q₀²−1). Its envelope is strictly convex in q, so only endpoints compete. On the vertex branch the envelope is −r²/16−z−r²/(16z), uniquely maximized at z=r/4 by AM–GM; there rq<4z strictly, so the junction has strictly smaller value. Compare the attained −r/2−r²/16 against the q=0 value −1 to get the exact crossing 4(√2−1) and only the two claimed ties. For r≥4 the vertex branch is absent since 2q²−1≤q; the competing endpoint q=1 gives 1−r<−1. Substitution gives the stated probability, and the unshifted derivative −sin φ(b+4c cos φ) gives two strict maxima for 0<r<4. The time conversion is 4.36868 hours at the crossing on a 24-hour period. value.rationale: The result resolves exactly when equal half-cycle spacing ceases to be optimal in a minimal model where both harmonics matter. The switch between two separated global designs is discontinuous and precedes the loss of the second intensity maximum; knowing the mere presence of two peaks cannot recover the optimal design. This is a meaningful model benchmark for robust timing, not a field prescription for real eDNA signals.
